question.problem: A writer is editing the first draft of a book. On average, there have been $2$ typos per page. What is the probability of finding at least $4$ typos on the next page? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that typos occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of typos on a page of the book. Since the average rate is $2$ typos per page, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of typos can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =2,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(2).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{2}^{x}{e}^{-2}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X\ge 4),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X\ge 4)=1-P(X<4)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\in {0,1,2,3}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =\frac{{2}^{0}{e}^{-2}}{0!}+\frac{{2}^{1}{e}^{-2}}{1!}+\frac{{2}^{2}{e}^{-2}}{2!}+\frac{{2}^{3}{e}^{-2}}{3!} \\  & ≈0.857\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of finding at least $4$ typos on the next page is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 4) & =1-P(X<4) \\  & ≈1-0.857 \\  & =0.143\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
